label: RADIUS
notes: RADIUS AAA (RFC 2865) over UDP: authentication on port 1812 and accounting (RFC 2866) on port 1813 share the same 20-byte fixed header, which is modelled here as code, identifier and length. The 16-byte authenticator inside the window is excluded: it is 16 random octets in a request and an MD5 digest over the packet in a reply, so it is both four times the 4-byte BPF load window and a per-packet cryptographic value with no stable bytes worth matching. Everything past byte 20 is the attribute chain — type, length, value triplets where each attribute's position depends on the lengths of all preceding ones — so no attribute byte sits at a fixed offset. Status-Server and Status-Client (RFC 5997) are bare 20-byte keepalive probes over the authentication port and reuse this header unchanged. The legacy ports 1645/1646 (pre-RFC-2865 deployments and some NAS defaults) carry the same layout but are not part of the locator; add them per deployment if needed. When the length field counts fewer octets than the UDP datagram carries, the extra octets are padding and must be ignored.

fields.label: Code
fields.description: Which RADIUS exchange the packet belongs to: codes 1-3 and 11 are the access exchanges of RFC 2865 section 4, codes 4-5 the accounting exchanges of RFC 2866 section 2, and codes 12-13 the keepalive probes of RFC 5997. A reply repeats the code semantics of its exchange (Access-Accept/Reject answer an Access-Request, Accounting-Response an Accounting-Request) rather than using a generic reply code.

fields.label: Identifier
fields.description: One-octet identifier chosen by the requester and echoed by the reply to pair the two halves of one exchange. Retransmissions reuse it; distinct concurrent requests must carry distinct in-flight identifiers so replies cannot be mismatched.

fields.label: Packet Length
fields.description: Total length of the RADIUS packet in octets, header and attribute chain included: the minimum 20 is a bare header, the maximum 4096 is the largest packet a receiver accepts. Octets between this length and the end of the UDP datagram are padding.

excluded.reason: 16-octet Request/Response Authenticator (16 random octets in a request, an MD5 digest over the packet in a reply) — four times the 4-byte BPF load window, and a per-packet cryptographic value with no stable bytes worth matching
